summary: Standard Fibonacci-calculated pivots preserve the Daily/H1 pivot-zone wick/terminal phenomenon on 2015-2021 but do not outperform classic pivots. Daily Fibonacci/H1 is robustly positive (+1.052 pp wick interaction, CI +0.634 to +1.473 pp). Weekly Fibonacci/H4 is directionally positive (+1.234 pp) but sits at the inference boundary (CI +0.012 to +2.441 pp; Holm p=0.0488) and is treated as borderline because the historical parent runner/terminal ledger is not available for exact byte-for-byte comparator replay. Paired Fibonacci-minus-Classic wick intervals include zero for both horizons, so formula superiority is not established.

robustness: Daily Fibonacci wick interaction is positive in both development (+1.292 pp) and validation (+0.456 pp).
Weekly Fibonacci wick interaction is positive in development (+1.480 pp) and validation (+0.614 pp).
Both Fibonacci core wick-severity gradients are monotonic increasing.
Paired formula-difference confidence intervals include zero on both horizons, rejecting any claim of Fibonacci superiority.
Corrected classic comparator primary wick interactions reproduce frozen parent headline effects within approximately 0.01 percentage point on both horizons.
limitations: The original heavy parent runner and terminal-event ledger were not committed; exact byte-for-byte classic comparator replay is therefore unavailable in the current environment.
The corrected reconstructed classic structural effect remains +0.103 pp above the frozen Daily/H1 parent and +0.066 pp above the frozen Weekly/H4 parent.
Weekly Fibonacci/H4 is inference-boundary evidence: its wick CI lower bound is only +0.012 pp and Holm p=0.0488, so the remaining reproduction limitation is scientifically material.
2022-2025 is not a pristine Fibonacci holdout because those years were already exposed for the related Daily/H1 classic-pivot question.
Structural midpoint study only; no executable BID/ASK strategy, entry, stop, target or P&L claim.
